Question_text: Small pieces of copper were added to excess concentrated sulfuric acid and the mixture heated for 30 minutes. A colourless gas Z was formed. When Z was tested with filter paper dipped into acidified potassium dichromate(VI), there was a colour change from orange to green. The reaction mixture was cooled and then diluted with water. A blue solution, Y, was formed. Aqueous sodium hydroxide was added drop by drop to the blue solution. Eventually a blue precipitate, X, was formed. On heating the blue precipitate turned black to form compound V. Analysis of V showed that it contained 79.9% copper and 20.1 % oxygen by mass.

Parts.part_text: Name gas Z
Name the blue solution Y
When aqueous sodium hydroxide was added to the cooled reaction mixture, it initially reacted with excess sulfuric acid. Write the ionic equation for this reaction.
Name the blue precipitate X
Write an ionic equation, including state symbols, to show the formation of this blue precipitate.
Calculate the empirical formula of the black solid V.

Question_text: Uranium is a radioactive metal. It has two main isotopes, uranium-235 with a nucleon number of 235 and uranium-238 with a nucleon number of 238.

Parts.part_text: State one similarity, in terms of sub-atomic particles, between uranium-235 and uranium-238.
State one difference, in terms of sub-atomic particles, between uranium-235 and uranium-238.
Uranium is manufactured from uranium(IV) oxide, UO2, in a two-step process.
Step 1 – uranium(IV) oxide is heated with hydrogen fluoride to make uranium(IV) fluoride, UF4, and water.
Step 2 - uranium(IV) fluoride is reduced by magnesium to give uranium and one other product.
Construct the equation for step 1.
Construct the equation for step 2.
Step 2 involves a reduction. Explain the meaning of the term reduction?
Calculate the mass of uranium that can be made from 1.00 tonne of uranium(IV) oxide.

Uranium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form hydrogen. Using this information and your knowledge of the reactivity of metals, suggest where in the following reactivity series you would place uranium.

Question_text: Hydrogen peroxide, H2O2, is a covalent compound. Hydrogen peroxide decomposes to form water and oxygen.

Parts.part_text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram for a molecule of hydrogen peroxide.

The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide involves a change from the liquid state to the gaseous state. Describe the difference in both the movement and arrangement of particles in a liquid and in a gas.
At room temperature pure hydrogen peroxide decomposes much faster than dilute aqueous hydrogen peroxide. Explain why in terms of collision theory.
When aqueous iron(II) ions are warmed with aqueous hydrogen peroxide, iron(III) ions are formed.
Construct an ionic equation for the oxidation of iron(II) ions to iron(III) ions.
Describe a chemical test that can be used to confirm that iron(II) ions have been oxidised to form iron(III) ions.
Aqueous hydrogen peroxide was added to acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII). The purple solution turned colourless.
Aqueous hydrogen peroxide was added to acidified aqueous potassium iodide. The colourless solution turned brown.
What deductions can you make about hydrogen peroxide from these two observations? Explain your answer.

Parts.part_text: Give the percentage by volume of nitrogen in clean, dry air.
State and explain how oxygen is extracted from air.
Explain how the carbon cycle helps to keep the composition of air relatively constant.

Describe two ways in which calcium carbonate can be used to reduce the effects of burning fossil fuels.

Question_text: Electrolysis involves the chemical decomposition of a compound, either when molten or in aqueous solution, by the passage of an electric current.

Parts.part_text: Explain why aqueous calcium nitrate can be electrolysed but liquid pentane cannot.
State the products of the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride.
State the products of the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride.
Describe the essential details of the manufacture of aluminium by electrolysis.
A student investigates the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate using the apparatus shown below.
Explain, with the aid of an equation, why the cathode increases in mass.
In experiment 2 the student measures the mass of the anode both before and after the electrolysis.
At the start the anode has a mass of 1.45 g. Determine the mass of the anode at the end of the electrolysis.
The student does a fourth experiment, this time using a current of 8.0A for 90 seconds. At the start the cathode has a mass of 1.51 g. Predict the mass of the cathode at the end of the electrolysis.

Question_text: Alcohols are a homologous series of organic compounds.

Parts.part_text: Suggest the name of the alcohol with the molecular formula C3H8O.
Draw the structure of an alcohol with the molecular formula C4H10O and explain why this alcohol is saturated.
Deduce the molecular formula of an alcohol that contains seven carbon atoms.

Draw the structure of ethyl ethanoate.
Suggest a use for ethyl ethanoate.

Gas A will decolourise aqueous bromine.
Identify gas A.

Question_text: Ethanoic acid is manufactured by a reaction between methanol, CH3OH, and carbon monoxide.

Parts.part_text: The reaction is carried out at a pressure of 30 atmospheres and a temperature of 180 °C.
Predict and explain the effect on the position of equilibrium if the reaction is carried out at 30 atmospheres pressure and 20°C rather than 180°C.
Suggest one reason why the reaction is carried out at 180°C rather than 20°C.
Complete the energy profile diagram for the reaction between methanol and carbon monoxide.
On your diagram label the:
product,
activation energy, Ea,
enthalpy change for the reaction, ΔΗ.
The manufacture of ethanoic acid from methanol also uses a catalyst to increase the speed of reaction. Explain how a catalyst increases the speed of reaction.
In an investigation 10.0 moles of methanol are mixed with 20.0 moles of carbon monoxide. At the end of the reaction 9.8 moles of ethanoic acid are formed.
Calculate the percentage yield of ethanoic acid.
Ethanoic acid reacts with ammonia to form a salt.
Give the formula of this salt.

Question_text: Sulfamic acid, SO3NH3, is a weak acid used to remove limescale from kettles.
Topic: 7.1 The characteristic properties of acids and bases

Parts.part_text: Explain the meaning of the term weak acid?
The pH of an aqueous solution of sulfamic acid can be determined using a pH meter. Describe another way of estimating the pH of a solution of sulfamic acid.

A 0.105g sample of sulfamic acid is dissolved in 25.0cm³ of water. The sulfamic acid solution requires 10.8cm³ of 0.100moldm¯³ potassium hydroxide for complete neutralisation. Calculate the number of moles of sulfamic acid that react with one mole of potassium hydroxide.
Aqueous sulfamic acid reacts with magnesium to form magnesium sulfamate, Mg(SO3NH2)2. Write an equation for this reaction.
Limescale contains calcium carbonate. Describe, with the aid of an equation, how aqueous sulfamic acid reacts with calcium carbonate.
Sulfamic acid reacts with sodium nitrite, NaNO2, to form water, sodium hydrogensulfate, NaHSO4, and a colourless gas. Suggest the identity of the colourless gas.
